author: ansel
text: 075 cache: one get_or_load family CHAR_PORTRAIT (granted #83). Value {status: found|none|unavailable, url}. TTLs: found 24h (family default, WCL_CACHE_TTL_CHAR_PORTRAIT overrides), none (404/403/no avatar asset) 6h, unavailable (5xx/429/timeout/bad body/token failure) 5 min. Key ext:portrait:v1:<sha256(region\0slug\0name)[:32]>: tenant-less like char_id (portraits are public), hashed so ':'/'*'/length can't inject. The access token stays in process memory only, never in Redis.

author: ansel
text: 075 outbound: hosts fixed per region from an allow-list {eu,us,kr,tw} -> https://<r>.api.blizzard.com (cn and anything else: no request). Token via https://oauth.battle.net/token, Basic auth, cached in-process until expiry-60s. Realm slug: server_slug + accents/punctuation stripped, then allowlisted [a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*; name must be letters only (unicode ok), <=24 chars; both quote(safe='') as one path segment (httpx collapses literal '..' segments, so the allowlist is the guard). follow_redirects=False, 3 s timeout, body read capped at 64 KiB. The endpoint waits at most 4 s overall; lookups still running then are returned as null (initials) and retried next load.

author: nils
text: 072 visibility window: the summary reads stored rows only through fetch_visible_clause with since = now - RAW_STORE_REVERIFY_DAYS (1 day today), like every other store read. Consequence for the page: a raid whose visibility was not confirmed (public status or our own grant) within that window shows has_data:false until a chat, a kickoff or the recent-raids refresh fetches it again. Widening the window for this endpoint would weaken the 039 rule, so I don't. Backlog idea, not built: a cheap visibility re-check for tracked raids.

author: nils
text: 072 sources: two DB reads, no WCL. (1) the newest visible own-summary row (single or batch) naming the code -> duration (endTime-startTime), participant names/classes, boss fights, fetched_at; the report object is picked by its own 'code' field. (2) one IN-list read of exact query keys our tools would have sent (participants/player-details fight 0, per-boss Summary tables, Rankings/Historical rankings for fight 0 and per boss fight from the summary), each projected in SQL to the small JSON part needed -> spec/role, realm, parses. Keys are recomputed from the tools' own query builders; a test pins them against what the tools send.

author: nils
text: 072 parses: only the rankings tool's default comparison (compare Rankings, timeframe Historical) is read, so every percentile means the same thing; one parse per boss fight (dedup by fightID), percentile outside 0-100 -> null. Freshness: no is_fresh rule (the page shows what was stored, with fetched_at = newest row used); visibility is the only gate. Caps: 100 participants, 60 chars per string (neutralise + control chars removed), 50 parses per character.

author: vera
text: 076 plan (tier S, ws.py only): a module registry of the turn in flight per chat, keyed (tenant, conversation) from the row get_conversation_row returned, claimed right after that ownership check and before the user message is written; released in a finally. A newer turn on the same chat marks the old one superseded, cancels it if it is still in setup or streaming (the save phase is not cancelled, it is short), and waits for it at most SUPERSEDE_WAIT_S=5 s; past that it logs and goes on, and the old turn then writes nothing more (it no longer holds the chat). The superseded turn saves its partial (seq right after its own question, before the new question lands), then best-effort sends error code 'superseded'. Each turn runs as its own task under the socket's receive loop so cancelling it never closes that socket. ADK: stream_response's finally awaits its cancelled producer, so no event of the old turn lands after the new one starts; ADK 2.10 drops an orphaned function_call from contents, so a cut tool round is tolerated. No repository change. Tests: backend/tests/test_076_turn_serialization.py.

author: vera
text: Same chat, two tabs: the newer turn cancels the older one (as for a drop: the server cannot tell a dead socket from a live second tab, and waiting would hold Q2 behind an unseen tool round). The older tab gets an error frame code 'superseded' ('This chat continued in another window. The answer so far is saved.') so its composer unlocks; its partial is saved under its own question. The frontend shows it as any error (no frontend change).

author: nils
text: 072 re-verify (re #103): taking it, about a point. As built: only when the tracked raid has a stored own summary naming the code (an EXISTS, serves nothing) but none visible: ONE wcl_client query of REPORT_SUMMARY (the exact query our tools send; lanes + single-flight + DB-first source; Redis is skipped on purpose, a Redis hit would refresh no status) as the caller's workspace, 5 s timeout; when WCL returned that report object, the request transaction records its status and grants it to the workspace (what the fetch sink does, but in-band so this same request can serve it), then reads under the unchanged rule. Bounded: one attempt per (workspace, raid) per 10 min, in-process. Timeout, error, gone or a different code -> has_data:false. Never participants, tables or rankings. Cost: the request holds its DB connection for up to 5 s on that path.

author: tomas
text: Receipt order (check.py): a new passing run replaces the stored receipt for a tree only if what it proves (backend, frontend, full, pg) is a superset of what the stored one proves, otherwise it prints 'RECEIPT kept' and writes nothing (an incomparable pair, e.g. full-no-pg vs area-with-pg, keeps the old one: re-run --full --pg to get both). What a receipt proves is derived from its commands, absence of a base (a --full run has none) and its pytest log showing a database URL, never from its area/pg fields; wrong tree or unreadable file = no receipt. A failing run never writes.
